question: A new joiner asks how the Claude model tiers differ from the point of view of someone using the Claude app. Which description is accurate?
options: A) Sonnet reasons most deeply, Opus is the everyday default option, and Haiku handles only images.
B) Haiku gives the deepest reasoning, Sonnet is the fastest option, and Opus suits routine bulk work.
C) Opus reasons most deeply and uses more allowance, Sonnet is the capable default, Haiku is fastest.
D) The tiers produce identical answers and differ only in how quickly those answers come back to you.
correct_answers: C) Opus reasons most deeply and uses more allowance, Sonnet is the capable default, Haiku is fastest.
explanations: Incorrect. Sonnet is the capable default rather than the deepest tier, and Haiku is a general fast model, not an image-only one.
Incorrect. This inverts the tiers. Haiku is the fastest and cheapest rather than the deepest-reasoning option.
Correct. As an end user experiences them, the tiers trade reasoning depth against speed and how much of the usage allowance each message consumes.
Incorrect. Speed is one axis, but reasoning depth genuinely differs, which is why the choice matters on hard work.
